sqrt.title: How f64::sqrt works
sqrt.description: The square root; NaN for negative numbers.

slides.caption: sqrt finds the number that, multiplied by itself, gives the input.
The root of 2 is irrational; f64 gives the closest double: 1.4142135623730951.
For integers, convert first: (n as f64).sqrt(). The square root of a negative number is NaN (not a number).

powi.title: How f64::powi works
powi.description: Raises a float to a whole-number power.

slides.caption: powi(10) multiplies the number by itself 10 times.
powi takes an i32 exponent and is faster than powf, which allows fractional exponents.

round.title: How f64::round works
round.description: Rounds to the nearest whole number; halves go away from zero.

slides.caption: round picks the nearest integer. Exact halves are rounded away from zero.
2.5 is exactly halfway: away from zero, 3.
-2.5 is halfway: away from zero means -3.
The result is still an f64 (3.0). Use round_ties_even for banker's rounding (2.5 → 2).

floor.title: How f64::floor works
floor.description: Rounds down to the next whole number (towards minus infinity).

slides.caption: floor goes down to the nearest integer below.
-2.7 goes down to -3, not -2: down means more negative.
ceil rounds up instead; trunc just drops the fraction (-2.7 → -2).

ceil.title: How f64::ceil works
ceil.description: Rounds up to the next whole number (towards plus infinity).

slides.caption: ceil goes up to the nearest integer above.
Useful for "how many pages for n items": (n as f64 / per_page as f64).ceil().

trunc.title: How f64::trunc works
trunc.description: Drops the fractional part, towards zero.

slides.caption: trunc simply removes everything after the decimal point.
Casting with as i32 also truncates: -2.7 as i32 is -2.

hypot.title: How f64::hypot works
hypot.description: The length of the long side of a right triangle: √(x² + y²).

slides.caption: hypot computes √(3² + 4²) without overflowing for large values.
The distance between two points: (x2 - x1).hypot(y2 - y1).

rem_euclid.title: How f64::rem_euclid works
rem_euclid.description: A remainder that is never negative.

slides.caption: % keeps the sign of the left side; rem_euclid always lands in 0..360.

exp.title: How f64::exp works
exp.description: e raised to the power x.

slides.caption: exp is the exponential function, used for growth and decay.
ln is its inverse: x.exp().ln() == x (up to rounding).
ln answers: e to which power gives x?
log10 and log2 use other bases; ln of 0 is -infinity, of a negative number NaN.

powf.title: How f64::powf works
powf.description: Raises a float to a float power.

slides.caption: powf accepts fractional exponents; powi only whole ones (and is faster).
Negative bases with fractional exponents give NaN.

cbrt.title: How f64::cbrt works
cbrt.description: The cube root: the number that, multiplied by itself three times, gives x.

slides.caption: Unlike sqrt, cube roots of negative numbers exist.

log10.title: How f64::log10 works
log10.description: The base-10 logarithm: how many times you multiply 10 to get x.

slides.caption: Decibels and the Richter scale use log10.
For integers, ilog2 avoids floats entirely.
log(b) answers: b to which power gives x?
log2, log10 and ln are more precise for their bases.
For integer powers of two, 1u64 << n is exact.

mul_add.title: How f64::mul_add works
mul_add.description: Computes x × a + b with a single rounding.

slides.caption: The multiplication and addition happen together, which can be more accurate.
Used in numeric code like polynomial evaluation.

exp_m1.title: How f64::exp_m1 works
exp_m1.description: eˣ - 1, accurate even for tiny x.

slides.caption: exp(x) - 1 loses digits for small x; exp_m1 keeps them.
For 1e-10 the answer is about 1e-10, kept precisely.
Used in finance and physics formulas with small rates.

ln_1p.title: How f64::ln_1p works
ln_1p.description: ln(1 + x), accurate even for tiny x.

slides.caption: Adding 1 first would lose the small digits.

fract.title: How f64::fract works
fract.description: The part after the decimal point.

slides.caption: fract keeps the sign of the number.

round_ties_even.title: How f64::round_ties_even works
round_ties_even.description: Rounds to the nearest whole number; exact halves go to the even neighbour.

slides.caption: round() always rounds halves away from zero; this avoids a bias in long sums.
Statistics and accounting often use this rule.

div_euclid.title: How f64::div_euclid works
div_euclid.description: Division rounded so that rem_euclid is never negative.

slides.caption: -7 / 2 = -3.5; div_euclid gives -4 so the remainder is +1.

sin.title: How f64::sin works
sin.description: The sine of an angle in radians.

slides.caption: sin gives the height of a point on the unit circle.
sin(π/2) = 1, the top of the circle.

cos.title: How f64::cos works
cos.description: The cosine of an angle in radians.

slides.caption: cos gives the horizontal position on the unit circle.
Circles: x = r * a.cos(), y = r * a.sin().

tan.title: How f64::tan works
tan.description: The tangent of an angle in radians: sin / cos.

slides.caption: tan is the slope of a line at that angle.
Floating-point gives 0.9999999999999999 for π/4; round for display.

atan2.title: How f64::atan2 works
atan2.description: The angle of the point (x, y), from -π to π.

slides.caption: Unlike atan(y / x), atan2 knows which quadrant the point is in.
The angle a game character must turn to face a target.

asin.title: How f64::asin works
asin.description: The angle whose sine is x (inverse sine).

slides.caption: Only values from -1 to 1 have an answer.

acos.title: How f64::acos works
acos.description: The angle whose cosine is x (inverse cosine).

slides.caption: The angle between two unit vectors is a.dot(b).acos().
NaN outside -1..=1; clamp the input first if rounding may push it over.

atan.title: How f64::atan works
atan.description: The angle whose tangent is x.

slides.caption: atan turns a slope back into an angle.

sin_cos.title: How f64::sin_cos works
sin_cos.description: Sine and cosine together, as a pair.

slides.caption: Often both are needed, e.g. to rotate a point.
let (s, c) = a.sin_cos(); then x' = x*c - y*s.
Hyperbolic functions appear in physics, like the shape of a hanging cable.
cosh and tanh are the related functions.

tanh.title: How f64::tanh works
tanh.description: The hyperbolic tangent: an S-curve from -1 to 1.

slides.caption: Large inputs get close to 1, very negative ones to -1.
A classic activation function in neural networks.
A hanging chain has the shape y = a·cosh(x / a).

f32-sqrt.title: How f32::sqrt works
f32-sqrt.description: The square root of a 32-bit float.

slides.caption: f32 is less precise than f64, but uses half the memory.

f32-powi.title: How f32::powi works
f32-powi.description: Raises an f32 to a whole-number power.

slides.caption: powi multiplies; it is faster than powf.

f32-powf.title: How f32::powf works
f32-powf.description: Raises an f32 to a float power.

slides.caption: Gamma correction in graphics uses c.powf(2.2).

f32-round.title: How f32::round works
f32-round.description: Rounds to the nearest whole number; halves go away from zero.

slides.caption: The result is still an f32.
Convert to an integer afterwards with as i32.

f32-floor.title: How f32::floor works
f32-floor.description: Rounds down to the whole number at or below.

slides.caption: floor always goes down, even for negatives.
Grid cell from a position: (pos / cell_size).floor().

f32-ceil.title: How f32::ceil works
f32-ceil.description: Rounds up to the whole number at or above.

f32-sin.title: How f32::sin works
f32-sin.description: The sine of an f32 angle in radians.

slides.caption: Same as f64::sin, with f32 precision.
Games often use f32 for speed and memory.

f32-cos.title: How f32::cos works
f32-cos.description: The cosine of an f32 angle in radians.

slides.caption: Same as f64::cos, with f32 precision.

f32-exp.title: How f32::exp works
f32-exp.description: e raised to the power x, for f32.

f32-ln.title: How f32::ln works
f32-ln.description: The natural logarithm of an f32.

slides.caption: ln(1) = 0 exactly. ln(e) should be 1, but e itself is rounded to fit in an f32.
ln(e) comes out as 0.99999994: f32 has only about 7 digits.
Never compare floats with ==; check (a - b).abs() < 1e-6. Negative inputs give NaN.

f32-log10.title: How f32::log10 works
f32-log10.description: The base-10 logarithm of an f32.

slides.caption: log2 and ln are the other common bases.

f32-atan2.title: How f32::atan2 works
f32-atan2.description: The angle of the point (x, y) for f32.

slides.caption: Straight up is a quarter turn: π/2.
The point is directly above the origin.
Games use it to aim at a target.

f32-trunc.title: How f32::trunc works
f32-trunc.description: Drops the fractional part (rounds towards zero).

slides.caption: Unlike floor, negative numbers go up.
x as i32 truncates the same way.

f32-fract.title: How f32::fract works
f32-fract.description: The part after the decimal point.

slides.caption: Keeps the sign of the input.
Useful for repeating animations: t.fract() loops from 0 to 1.

f32-hypot.title: How f32::hypot works
f32-hypot.description: √(x² + y²) for f32: the length of a 2D vector.

f32-cbrt.title: How f32::cbrt works
f32-cbrt.description: The cube root of an f32.

f32-tan.title: How f32::tan works
f32-tan.description: The tangent of an f32 angle in radians.

slides.caption: Near π/2 the value shoots towards infinity.

f32-mul_add.title: How f32::mul_add works
f32-mul_add.description: x × a + b with one rounding, for f32.

slides.caption: One rounding step instead of two.
Common in graphics shaders and physics.

f32-rem_euclid.title: How f32::rem_euclid works
f32-rem_euclid.description: A remainder that is never negative, for f32.
